subject: chemistry
question_text: Explain what happens when boric acid is heated.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: 370 K gives metaboric acid
lines: On heating to 370 K, orthoboric acid
H₃BO₃ loses one water molecule and gives
steps.why: Heating removes water in stages. The first stage is at 370 K, where each H₃BO₃ unit loses one water molecule and becomes metaboric acid HBO₂.
common_mistakes: Giving B₂O₃ as the product of the first stage. Boric oxide is formed only on stronger heating.
Leaving the water molecule off the right side of the equation.
steps.memory_tip: First water out at 370 K gives metaboric acid HBO₂.
steps.margin_note: 370 K is the temperature to write; describe the later stages without a number.

steps.label: Further heating gives boric oxide
lines: On further heating metaboric acid HBO₂
changes to tetraboric acid, and at red
heat this gives boric oxide B₂O₃:
steps.why: Strong heating drives the loss of water all the way to boric oxide B₂O₃. The overall equation gathers the stages into one line: two units of boric acid lose three water molecules in all.
common_mistakes: Writing tetraboric acid as H₂B₃O₇. The formula is H₂B₄O₇, with four boron atoms.
Stopping at metaboric acid. Strong heating carries the change on to B₂O₃.
steps.memory_tip: Water leaves in stages and boric oxide is what is left: 2H₃BO₃ → B₂O₃ + 3H₂O.
steps.margin_note: Write the overall equation as well as the stages.

insider_note: Both the stagewise equations and the overall equation are worth writing, because the overall line is what shows the three water molecules that leave altogether.
